extracted.intended_audience: readers of The New Yorker who submit, rate, or vote in the Cartoon Caption Contest
extracted.subtask_description: Participate in The New Yorker’s online Cartoon Caption Contest by submitting a caption, rating reader submissions, and voting on finalists; readers’ ratings select finalists and votes determine the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit Your Caption
rubrics_metrics.description: "Your caption for Contest #990 will be rated by readers, like you, in the next round.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement: submit a caption tied to the contest number; submitted captions are moved into a reader-rating round (no additional submission rules shown on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate Submissions (reader judging)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Your responses will help us select three finalists for Contest #989.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rating interface shown on the page with the options: "Unfunny", "Somewhat funny", "Funny". Note: "Sign in to rate captions." Ratings by readers are used to choose three finalists for the next stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vote on Finalists (reader voting)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Your choice will help determine the winning caption for Contest #988.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After finalists are selected, readers vote among finalists to determine the winner. The page emphasizes that reader choice determines the winning caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of winning/placed captions (illustrative standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Winner and runners-up for Contest #986 are shown as examples of successful captions: Winner — “I know a guy who’ll take Greenland off your hands if that helps.” (William Conway, Toronto, Ont.); Second Place — “Are you sweating or is that just the ice caps melting?” (Vijay Iyengar, Greenville, Del.); Third Place — “That’s what you get for trying to cancel your membership.” (Janet Snyder, Plano, Texas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These published winners serve as exemplars of captions that have succeeded in the contest; no explicit stylistic rules are given on the page, but the examples illustrate the sort of short, witty lines that have been selected as winner/placed captions.
